title: Prenatal exposure to organophosphate pesticides and neurobehavioral development of neonates: a birth cohort study in Shenyang, China.
ehr_evidence: Information on each subject was obtained by questionnaire. Dialkyl phosphate (DAP) metabolites were detected in the urine of mothers during pregnancy to evaluate the exposure level to OPs.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study assessing the association between prenatal organophosphate pesticide exposure (urinary DAP metabolites) and neonatal neurobehavioral development (NBNA scores) in Shenyang, China.
key_findings: A 10-fold increase in total DAP concentration was associated with a decrease of 1.78 in NBNA Summary scores (95% CI, -2.12 to -1.45).
Neonates in the highest quintile of prenatal OP exposure had an estimated 2.11-point lower summary NBNA score compared to the lowest quintile.
Maternal OP exposure was the strongest risk factor for lower NBNA scores among tested prenatal factors.
captured_features: Urinary DAP metabolites (DMP, DMTP, DEP, DETP, DEDTP)
population: 249 pregnant women and their neonates in Shenyang, China
exposure_domain: Organophosphate pesticide exposure (urinary dialkyl phosphate metabolites)
limitations: Single time-point urine measurement reflecting only recent exposure
Urinary DAPs cannot quantify exposure to specific pesticides
